page: Amazon Web Services r8gd.metal-48xl is a bare-metal, memory-optimized server powered by AWS ARMv9 Graviton Neoverse-V2 processors. The system delivers 192 dedicated physical cores operating at 2.7 GHz with a 1:1 core-to-thread ratio, lacking simultaneous multithreading (SMT). It is equipped with 1536.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory, translating to 8.0 GB per physical core. Built for large data footprints requiring direct hardware access, the server also bundles 11,400 GB of high-throughput local NVMe SSD storage and provides a baseline network throughput of 50 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluation shows top-tier multi-threaded processing capacity alongside massive memory throughput. Tests reflect a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 305,702.07 and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression throughput of 1,327.46 GB/sec, placing it in the top 10% of tested instances. The memory subsystem records 895.65 GB/sec uncached read bandwidth and 412.94 GB/sec write bandwidth. Conversely, single-threaded execution remains average, as demonstrated by a single-core Geekbench score of 1,660.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1,648.5.

Without hardware GPU acceleration, LLM inference text generation exhibits lower throughput, recording 50.14 tokens/sec on 135M parameter models and 2.87 tokens/sec on 70B models. However, the server excels at in-memory caching and transactional data workloads, achieving 374.08 million Redis SET operations per second and top-tier PassMark database operations scores. The integration of 11.4 TB NVMe local storage complements the massive RAM capacity, optimizing raw resource density and qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound applications without virtualization overhead.

The r8gd.metal-48xl is architected for large-scale enterprise deployments requiring high parallelism, extensive memory capacities, and fast scratch disk I/O. Its primary fit covers in-memory databases like Redis, real-time data streaming pipelines, massive code compilation tasks, large analytics processing clusters, and high-concurrency static web serving.

Offering an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio, it includes 11,400 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and 50 Gbps baseline networking without virtualization overhead. Benchmark profiles reveal exceptional multi-core throughput and top-tier memory bandwidth, achieving 374.08 million Redis SET operations per second and high-end software compilation speeds. While single-thread execution and CPU-only LLM token generation are modest, its massive core count, high-speed RAM, and dense local storage provide significant cost efficiency for heavy, parallel in-memory workloads. It is purpose-built for enterprise in-memory databases, real-time analytics, large-scale caching layers, and high-throughput transactional processing.
